result.summary: This PR changes DiscourageFeeSniping and the bumpfee (CreateRateBumpTransaction) code path so that a fee-bumped replacement transaction's locktime is never set below the original transaction's locktime, adding a new minimum_height parameter to CoinControl and DiscourageFeeSniping. It closes issue #26526, where bitcoind's anti-fee-sniping locktime randomization could occasionally 'backdate' a replacement transaction's locktime below the original's, creating a wallet fingerprint. The PR includes new unit tests in feebumper_tests.cpp and spend_tests.cpp validating the bounds of the new logic including stale-chain and out-of-range minimum_height cases.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core's anti-fee-sniping locktime randomization can occasionally produce a bumpfee replacement transaction with a locktime older than the transaction it replaces, an unusual and unrealistic pattern that observers can use to fingerprint the transaction as coming from Core or Electrum's bumpfee feature. This affects privacy-conscious wallet users who use RBF fee bumping, though the author's data analysis shows it affects under 2% of replaced RBF transactions.

resolved_concerns: Off-by-one error in the backdating range calculation (nervana21), fixed by author in a later push
Missing handling for stale-chain plus minimum_height-above-tip cases (molnard, nervana21), fixed by author
Architectural question of whether the invariant belongs in CCoinControl/DiscourageFeeSniping vs feebumper.cpp (molnard proposed alternative); molnard ultimately agreed author's approach fits better
Weak/flaky functional test (polespinasa, molnard) replaced with deterministic unit tests using a fixed RNG seed
Test bound errors (block_height-100 vs block_height-99) identified by molnard and fixed by author
Various commit message typos and code style nits, all addressed

categories.evidence: The PR modifies wallet-internal CoinControl, feebumper.cpp, and spend.cpp logic governing fee-bumping and anti-fee-sniping locktime behavior, core wallet transaction-construction code.
categories.rationale: Fixes a real but narrow privacy leak in bumpfee's locktime handling that could fingerprint replacement transactions as coming from Core/Electrum bumpfee. The author's own data analysis states 'on average there are only about 200-300 hundred replacements backdating per week... less than 2% of all the transactions that have been replaced', indicating real but modest-value user impact, mainly felt by privacy-conscious RBF users rather than the broader wallet user base.

No maintainer (non-contributor) has yet reviewed; all engaged reviewers are CONTRIBUTOR-level, so broader project consensus on merging is not yet established.
result.card: This PR fixes a wallet privacy leak where Bitcoin Core's bumpfee RBF replacement could get a locktime older than the original transaction's, due to anti-fee-sniping's random backdating, making such replacements fingerprintable as Core/Electrum bumpfee traffic (closes #26526). The author's data shows this affects under 2% of RBF replacements weekly, a real but narrow privacy issue affecting fee-bumping users. The PR went through extensive review across many weeks, with reviewers molnard, nervana21, and polespinasa raising and getting fixed several off-by-one and edge-case bugs (stale tip, minimum_height above block_height) and a considered-but-rejected architectural alternative. It now has ACK from molnard and tACK from nervana21 on the latest commit, with no open objections, and the author has been consistently responsive. No dependencies on other PRs are noted.
